text:
Maria: quick follow-up from today's all-hands — small set of clarifying q's on the mission + competitors, want to make sure our answers are consistent for field teams

Ashley: go for it, Maria. happy to answer.

Maria: thanks — first: when we say our mission is to make inference 'accessible' are we primarily talking about cost/latency for engineering teams, or also ease-of-integration (+ prebuilt connectors)?

Ashley: both, but prioritize developer velocity + predictable economics. accessibility = low friction onboarding (SDKs, docs) + guarantees you can run at scale without surprise costs. connectors are important for enterprise adoption but velocity is the initial hook.

Sam: technical nuance — we also mean "accessible" across infra: hosted for fast start, Dedicated for predictable throughput, Private for regulated stacks. same API surface across all three.

Maria: got it. second: how do we explain our position vs hyperscalers who offer model endpoints + raw GPUs? sales teams want a 1-2 sentence soundbite.

Kai: the field asked this a ton. my go-to: "Hyperscalers give you GPUs; we give you an inference platform optimized for production LLMs — predictable latency, built-in fallbacks, and operational tooling that saves dev time and per-token cost."

Ashley: succinct version: "We turn model serving from a project into a product."

Devon: can we add a note about model/catalog + performance validation? Customers ask why not just self-host an open model.

Sam: add: "We curate model variants, run perf profiles, and auto-select kernels/quantization to hit SLOs — it's not just hosting models, it's serving them well."

Maria: perfect. third: competition — when a customer asks difference vs startups that ship simple APIs (convenience focused), what do we say?

Ashley: emphasize production guarantees. "If you want to ship an MVP fast, many APIs work. If you need SLA, predictable costs, and runbooks that survive traffic spikes, we are built for that."

Jess: can we cite features like canary rollouts, per-route tracing, and KV caching as tangible evidence? engineers resonate with specifics.

Kai: sales will love that. also call out Dedicated and Private as mitigations for security/compliance objections.

Maria: last: are there any new shifts in roadmap or messaging leadership wants on the public site or decks?

Ashley: two small shifts: 1) move "cost controls" up the page — customers are increasingly cost-sensitive; 2) call out "unified runtime" as a headline benefit (same API across modes).

Sam: ops takeaway: we should publish a short tech note about kernel selection + quantization that marketing can reference.

Devon: i'll schedule a 30m alignment session tomorrow to update the site copy and one-pager.

Maria: awesome. one micro ask — can leadership provide a one-paragraph quote on "why Redwood" we can drop into sales decks?

Ashley: sure — "Redwood Inference makes inference predictable and economical so engineering teams can ship LLM features without building and operating the serving stack themselves. We focus on latency, cost, and reliability so customers can focus on product."

Kai: i'll plug that into the battlecards. thanks. :thumbsup:

Jess: small engineer Q — any guidance on when to pick Dedicated vs Dedicated+Burst?

Sam: rule of thumb: Dedicated for stable, high-throughput workloads where SLOs matter. Burst if you have infrequent spikes and want to avoid constant reserved cost. we'll add a short matrix to the docs.

OpsBot: Reminder: all-hands recording + slides uploaded to #resources/all-hands (link)

Maria: thanks everyone — closing this thread after we get the one-paragraph and the tech note link.

Ashley: great thread. appreciate the practical questions.

Kai: leaving a note to ops: prioritize updated site hero this week.

Maria: noted. closing. :white_check_mark:
